name: Salesforce
tagline: A configurable CRM platform to evaluate for customer processes, reporting and cross-team workflows.
description: Salesforce is a CRM platform to evaluate when customer processes require structured records, automation and cross-team reporting. The fit depends on the products and edition selected, data governance, implementation capacity and integration needs; current prices and ratings are not verified here.
pros: A documented sales workflow can be mapped to records, stages and ownership rules.
Complex reporting and automation requirements can be tested before a wider rollout.
A pilot helps reveal data governance and implementation work.
cons: Configuration and ongoing administration can be substantial for complex deployments.
Different products and editions should not be treated as interchangeable.
Migration, integration and renewal scope need written confirmation.

content.title: Define the customer process
content.body: Map the process from lead or enquiry through qualification, opportunity, close and handoff. Include renewals or service if required. Decide which system owns each record and which fields are mandatory before configuring the CRM.

content.title: Configuration and governance
content.body: Test a small set of record types, stages, permissions and automations. Assign owners for changes and establish a review process for fields and rules. Over-customization can create maintenance work and confusing user experiences.

content.title: Data quality and reporting
content.body: Import a controlled sample and test deduplication, ownership, required fields and history. Build the forecast or pipeline report the business actually uses and document definitions. Check that reports remain consistent after a stage or ownership change.

content.title: Integration and access
content.body: List the systems that must exchange customer, product, billing or support data. Test failed syncs and duplicate updates. Review role permissions, audit history, export and offboarding before loading sensitive customer information.

content.title: Implementation and cost
content.body: Request a scoped proposal that separates licenses, implementation, integration, training, support and ongoing administration. Confirm renewal, cancellation and data export terms in writing; current prices and plan limits are not independently verified here.

faqs.question: Who should evaluate Salesforce?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Salesforce when its primary workflow matches a documented requirement. Run a representative pilot and verify current capabilities, limits and contract terms directly with the vendor.

faqs.question: Are prices and ratings independently verified here?
faqs.answer: No. This review does not present an independently verified price or third-party rating. Check current official documentation and obtain a dated quote.

faqs.question: What should a pilot include?
faqs.answer: Test the main workflow, one failure case, permissions, integrations, export and offboarding. Record pass, partial pass, fail or unknown and assign an owner to every unresolved requirement.

faqs.question: How should total cost be compared?
faqs.answer: Include licenses, usage, implementation, migration, training, integrations, support, internal administration and renewal terms—not only the headline subscription.

author: Sarah Chen
learningCurve: Steep — requires dedicated training time for full proficiency
whoShouldUse: Salesforce is designed for fast-growing startups that need a scalable crm & sales platform. Its generous free tier and flexible pricing make it accessible for early-stage companies.
whoShouldNotUse: Salesforce may be overwhelming for users who only need basic crm & sales functionality. Its extensive feature set can create unnecessary complexity for simple use cases.
